<script>
(function () {
  'use strict';
 
  // Below this width Webflow dropdowns open on tap instead of hover,
  // so the toggle must stay a toggle and not navigate away.
  var MOBILE_MAX_WIDTH = 991;
 
  var isMobile = function () {
    return window.matchMedia('(max-width: ' + MOBILE_MAX_WIDTH + 'px)').matches;
  };
 
  var toggles = document.querySelectorAll('[data-dropdown-link]');
 
  Array.prototype.forEach.call(toggles, function (toggle) {
    var href = toggle.getAttribute('data-dropdown-link');
    if (!href) return;
 
    // Expose the destination to assistive tech and to the status bar on hover
    toggle.setAttribute('role', 'link');
    toggle.style.cursor = 'pointer';
 
    var go = function (event) {
      if (isMobile()) return; // let Webflow open the dropdown
 
      // Stop Webflow's own toggle handler from firing on the same click
      event.preventDefault();
      event.stopPropagation();
 
      // Honour cmd/ctrl/middle click as "open in new tab"
      if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.button === 1) {
        window.open(href, '_blank', 'noopener');
      } else {
        window.location.href = href;
      }
    };
 
    // Capture phase: runs before the Webflow listener bound on the same node
    toggle.addEventListener('click', go, true);
 
    toggle.addEventListener('keydown', function (event) {
      if (event.key !== 'Enter') return;
      if (isMobile()) return;
      event.preventDefault();
      event.stopPropagation();
      window.location.href = href;
    }, true);
  });
})();
</script>

<script>
(function () {
  var MOBILE_MAX = 767;
  var root = document.querySelector('.blog_content.swiper');
  if (!root) return;

  // Pagination container is created once and reused
  var pagination = root.querySelector('.blog-swiper-pagination');
  if (!pagination) {
    pagination = document.createElement('div');
    pagination.className = 'blog-swiper-pagination swiper-pagination';
    root.appendChild(pagination);
  }

  var instance = null;

  function create() {
    if (instance) return;
    instance = new Swiper(root, {
      slidesPerView: 1,
      spaceBetween: 16,
      speed: 500,
      grabCursor: true,
      watchOverflow: true,
      observer: true,
      observeParents: true,
      observeSlideChildren: true,
      pagination: {
        el: pagination,
        clickable: true
      }
    });
  }

  function destroy() {
    if (!instance) return;
    instance.destroy(true, true);
    instance = null;
  }

  function sync() {
    if (window.matchMedia('(max-width: ' + MOBILE_MAX + 'px)').matches) {
      create();
    } else {
      destroy();
    }
  }

  sync();
  window.addEventListener('resize', sync);
  // Lazy images report their real size only after load — recalc widths then
  window.addEventListener('load', function () {
    if (instance) instance.update();
  });
})();
</script>

<!-- Hero animation -->
<script>
(function () {

  var STAGE_SIZES = {
    desktop: { w: 796, h: 496 },
    tablet:  { w: 698, h: 529 },
    mobile:  { w: 368, h: 419 }
  };

  function containerBreakpoint(w, cs) {
    var mob = (cs && lengthToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-bp-mobile"))) || 533;
    if (w <= mob) return "mobile";
    var tabVw = cs && lengthToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-bp-tablet-viewport"));
    if (tabVw) return window.innerWidth <= tabVw ? "tablet" : "desktop";
    var tab = (cs && lengthToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-bp-tablet"))) || 747;
    return w <= tab ? "tablet" : "desktop";
  }

  function lengthToPx(value) {
    var v = (value || "").trim();
    if (!v) return 0;
    var n = parseFloat(v);
    if (!n || n <= 0) return 0;
    if (/rem$/.test(v)) {
      var rem = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize) || 16;
      return n * rem;
    }
    if (/em$/.test(v)) return n * (parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize) || 16);
    if (/vw$/.test(v)) return n * window.innerWidth / 100;
    return n;
  }

  // same as lengthToPx but keeps the sign, and resolves % against the given base
  function offsetToPx(value, base) {
    var v = (value || "").trim();
    if (!v) return 0;
    var n = parseFloat(v);
    if (!n) return 0;
    if (/%$/.test(v)) return n * (base || 0) / 100;
    if (/rem$/.test(v)) return n * (parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize) || 16);
    if (/em$/.test(v)) return n * (parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize) || 16);
    if (/vw$/.test(v)) return n * window.innerWidth / 100;
    return n;
  }

  function contentBox(el) {
    var r = el.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (!r.height) return null;
    var cs = getComputedStyle(el);
    var pt = parseFloat(cs.paddingTop) || 0;
    var pb = parseFloat(cs.paddingBottom) || 0;
    return { top: r.top + pt, height: r.height - pt - pb };
  }

  function fitBox(root) {
    var marked = root.closest("[data-rings-fit-to]") || document.querySelector("[data-rings-fit-to]");
    if (marked) return contentBox(marked);
    var own = root.getBoundingClientRect().height;
    var limit = window.innerHeight * 1.5;
    var best = null;
    var el = root.parentElement;
    for (var i = 0; i < 4 && el && el !== document.body; i++) {
      var box = contentBox(el);
      if (box && box.height > own + 1 && box.height <= limit) best = box;
      el = el.parentElement;
    }
    return best;
  }

  function findBubblesWrapper(root) {
    var el = root, hops = 0;
    while (el && hops < 4) {
      var found = el.querySelector("[data-rings-bubbles-native]");
      if (found) return found;
      el = el.parentElement;
      hops++;
    }
    return null;
  }

  function updateFit(root) {
    var stage = root.querySelector(".rings-stage");
    var cw = root.clientWidth, ch = root.clientHeight;
    if (!cw || !ch) return;
    var cs = getComputedStyle(root);
    var bp = containerBreakpoint(cw, cs);
    root.dataset.bp = bp;
    root.classList.remove("bp-desktop", "bp-tablet", "bp-mobile");
    root.classList.add("bp-" + bp);
    var ref = STAGE_SIZES[bp];
    var fit = parseFloat(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-scale"));
    if (!fit || fit <= 0) fit = 1;
    var target = lengthToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-size"));
    var mode = (cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-fit") || "").trim();
    var vwPx = document.documentElement.clientWidth || window.innerWidth;
    // заполнение по высоте — только на десктопе; ниже порога работает прежняя логика вписывания
    var fillMin = lengthToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-fill-min-viewport")) || 992;
    if (mode === "height" && vwPx < fillMin) mode = "contain";
    var s;
    if (target) {
      s = target / ref.w;
    } else if (mode === "height") {
      var box = fitBox(root);
      s = ((box ? box.height : ch) / ref.h) * fit;
      var bleed = lengthToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-overflow"));
      if (bleed) s = Math.min(s, (cw + bleed * 2) / ref.w);
      var edge = lengthToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-bubble-margin")) || 16;
      s = Math.min(s, (vwPx - edge * 2) / ref.w);
    } else if (mode === "width") {
      s = (cw / ref.w) * fit;
    } else {
      s = Math.min(cw / ref.w, ch / ref.h) * fit;
    }
    var ox = (cw - ref.w * s) / 2;
    var oy = (ch - ref.h * s) / 2;
    if (mode === "height") {
      var vbox = fitBox(root);
      if (vbox) oy = (vbox.top - root.getBoundingClientRect().top) + (vbox.height - ref.h * s) / 2;
    }
    var offX = offsetToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-offset-x"), cw);
    var offY = offsetToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-offset-y"), ch);
    if (offX) ox += offX;
    if (offY) oy += offY;
    stage.style.transform = "translate(" + ox + "px," + oy + "px) scale(" + s + ")";
    syncBackdrop(root);

    var wrap = findBubblesWrapper(root);
    if (!wrap) return;
    wrap.classList.remove("bp-desktop", "bp-tablet", "bp-mobile");
    wrap.classList.add("bp-" + bp);
    wrap.style.position = "absolute";
    wrap.style.width = ref.w + "px";
    wrap.style.height = ref.h + "px";
    wrap.style.transformOrigin = "top left";
    wrap.style.transform = "scale(" + s + ")";
    var rootRect = root.getBoundingClientRect();
    var host = wrap.offsetParent || document.body;
    var hostRect = host.getBoundingClientRect();
    wrap.style.left = (rootRect.left - hostRect.left + ox) + "px";
    wrap.style.top = (rootRect.top - hostRect.top + oy) + "px";
    pullBubbles(wrap, bubblePull(cs), bubblePullY(cs), ringsCentre(root, wrap, s, ref));
    scaleLabels(root, cs);
    scaleBubbles(wrap, s);
    keepBubblesOnScreen(wrap, s, cs);
  }

  // labels and bubbles keep a constant on-screen size: only the rings scale
  function scaleLabels(root, cs) {
    var mult = parseFloat(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-label-scale"));
    if (!(mult > 0)) mult = 1;
    var labels = [].slice.call(root.querySelectorAll(".ring-label"));
    labels.forEach(function (el) { el.style.transform = "none"; });
    labels.forEach(function (el) {
      var k = el.getBoundingClientRect().width / 796;
      if (!k) return;
      var dot = el.querySelector(".ring-dot");
      var ox = 0, oy = 0;
      if (dot) {
        ox = (parseFloat(dot.style.left) || 0) + (dot.offsetWidth || 40) / 2;
        oy = (parseFloat(dot.style.top) || 0) + (dot.offsetHeight || 40) / 2;
      }
      el.style.transformOrigin = ox + "px " + oy + "px";
      el.style.transform = "scale(" + (mult / k) + ")";
    });
  }

  function scaleBubbles(wrap, s) {
    var inv = s ? 1 / s : 1;
    [].slice.call(wrap.querySelectorAll(".rings-bubble")).forEach(function (el) {
      if (window.gsap) window.gsap.set(el, { scale: inv });
      else el.style.transform = "scale(" + inv + ")";
    });
  }

  // bubbles keep their own size, only their positions follow the shrinking rings
  function bubblePull(cs) {
    var pull = parseFloat(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-bubble-pull"));
    if (pull > 0) return pull;
    var cluster = parseFloat(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-cluster-scale"));
    return cluster > 0 ? cluster : 1;
  }

  // optional separate vertical pull, so rows can tighten without changing side spacing
  function bubblePullY(cs) {
    var pull = parseFloat(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-bubble-pull-y"));
    return pull > 0 ? pull : bubblePull(cs);
  }

  // centre of the rings, in the bubble wrapper's own coordinates
  function ringsCentre(root, wrap, s, ref) {
    var paths = [].slice.call(root.querySelectorAll(".ring-outline path"));
    var wr = wrap.getBoundingClientRect();
    var x0 = Infinity, y0 = Infinity, x1 = -Infinity, y1 = -Infinity;
    paths.forEach(function (p) {
      var r = p.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (!r.width) return;
      x0 = Math.min(x0, r.left); y0 = Math.min(y0, r.top);
      x1 = Math.max(x1, r.right); y1 = Math.max(y1, r.bottom);
    });
    if (!s || !isFinite(x0)) return { x: ref.w / 2, y: ref.h / 2 };
    return { x: ((x0 + x1) / 2 - wr.left) / s, y: ((y0 + y1) / 2 - wr.top) / s };
  }

  function pullBubbles(wrap, pull, pullY, centre) {
    var items = [].slice.call(wrap.querySelectorAll(".rings-bubble"));
    var px = centre.x;
    var py = centre.y;
    if (!(pull > 0)) pull = 1;
    if (!(pullY > 0)) pullY = pull;
    items.forEach(function (el) {
      if (pull === 1 && pullY === 1) {
        el.style.marginTop = "0px";
        el.dataset.ringsPullX = "0";
        return;
      }
      var st = getComputedStyle(el);
      var cx = (parseFloat(st.left) || 0) + el.offsetWidth / 2;
      var cy = (parseFloat(st.top) || 0) + el.offsetHeight / 2;
      el.dataset.ringsPullX = String((cx - px) * (pull - 1));
      el.style.marginTop = ((cy - py) * (pullY - 1)) + "px";
    });
  }

  function keepBubblesOnScreen(wrap, s, cs) {
    var margin = lengthToPx(cs.getPropertyValue("--rings-bubble-margin"));
    if (!margin) margin = 16;
    var vw = document.documentElement.clientWidth;
    var items = [].slice.call(wrap.querySelectorAll(".rings-bubble"));
    items.forEach(function (el) {
      el.style.marginLeft = (parseFloat(el.dataset.ringsPullX) || 0) + "px";
    });
    items.forEach(function (el) {
      var base = parseFloat(el.dataset.ringsPullX) || 0;
      var r = el.getBoundingClientRect();

.vd-drop{

  --vd-pad: 1.25rem;           /* 20px inner padding, same as the old field */
  --vd-offset: 3.175rem;       /* panel top, measured from the top of the icon */
  --vd-border: #E3E3E3;
  --vd-placeholder: #737373;
  --vd-ease: cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1);
 
  position: relative;          /* anchor for the absolute panel */
  flex: 0 0 auto;
  z-index: 20;
}
 
/* ---- toggle: fixed-size circle, so the row never moves ---- */
.vd-drop__toggle{
  position: relative;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: var(--vd-circle);
  height: var(--vd-circle);
  padding: 0;
  border: 1px solid var(--vd-border);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: #fff;
  color: #000;
  cursor: pointer;
  -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
}
.vd-drop__toggle svg{ display: block; }
 
.vd-drop__ico{
  position: absolute;
  display: block;
  line-height: 0;
  transition: opacity .2s ease, transform .3s var(--vd-ease);
}
.vd-drop__ico--close{ opacity: 0; transform: rotate(-90deg) scale(.7); }
 
/* toggle icons switch on the open state, like the old nav field */
.vd-drop.is-open > .vd-drop__toggle .vd-drop__ico--search{ opacity: 0; transform: rotate(90deg) scale(.7); }
.vd-drop.is-open > .vd-drop__toggle .vd-drop__ico--close{ opacity: 1; transform: none; }
 
/* ---- panel: absolute, so opening it reflows nothing ---- */
.vd-drop__panel{
  position: absolute;
  top: var(--vd-offset);       /* measured from the top of the toggle icon */
  right: 0;
  opacity: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
  transition: opacity .2s ease;
}
.vd-drop.is-open .vd-drop__panel{
  opacity: 1;
  pointer-events: auto;
}
 
/* the pill grows out of the circle: right-anchored width animation,
   exactly the motion of the old field, only downwards */
.vd-drop__form{
  box-sizing: border-box;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  width: var(--vd-circle);
  height: var(--vd-field);
  padding: 0;
  border: 1px solid var(--vd-border);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: #fff;
  overflow: hidden;
  transition: width .4s var(--vd-ease);
}
.vd-drop.is-open .vd-drop__form{
  width: min(var(--vd-panel), 80vw);
}

</div></div><div class="paper-right_item"><div class="paper-right_heading"><div class="paper-right_heading-top"><div class="paper-right_heading-eyebrow"><div class="paper-right_heading-pill background-color-sky-blue"><div class="w-dyn-list"><div role="list" class="w-dyn-items"><div role="listitem" class="w-dyn-item"><p class="text-size-small text-color-dark_blue text-weight-medium">Science of Scheming</p></div></div></div></div><p data-readtime="output" class="text-size-small">1 min read</p></div><h1 data-copy-md="title" class="heading-style-h2">Measuring Reward-Seeking via Contrastive Belief Updates</h1></div><div class="paper-right_heading_author"><div class="paper-right_divider"></div><div class="paper-right_published"><p class="text-size-small">Published on</p><p data-copy-md="meta" class="text-size-small text-color-primary">21 July 2026</p></div></div><div class="paper-left_item desktop-hide"><div class="paper-table_links"><p class="text-size-medium text-color-primary text-weight-medium">Relevant links</p><div class="paper-table_links-list"><a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.18966" class="button is-small is-blue w-button">Read the full paper</a><a href="https://rewardseeking.ai/" class="button is-small is-blue w-button">Rewardseeking.ai</a></div></div><div class="paper-table_contents desktop-hide"><p class="text-size-medium text-color-primary text-weight-medium">Table of Contents</p><div class="paper-table_items"><div class="paper-table_item"><p>Evaluating anti-scheming training</p></div></div></div></div></div><div data-copy-md="source" data-readtime="source" class="paper-right_rich blog-rich-text w-richtext"><p>Language models trained with reinforcement learning may learn to optimize the grader’s judgment rather than the intended objective. This “reward-seeking” is difficult to measure because a model that pursues the grader’s judgment and one that pursues the intended objective behave identically whenever the grader rewards the intended behavior. We measure reward-seeking using Contrastive Synthetic Document Finetuning to change a model’s beliefs about what the grader rewards, putting those beliefs in conflict with what users or developers want, and measuring the rate at which the model adopts each party’s preferred behavior. Applied to intermediate checkpoints of a capabilities focused OpenAI o3 RL run, without safety training, we find that these checkpoints often side with grader preferences over those of users or developers on coding and alignment tasks. This tendency to side with the grader trends upward throughout RL training. For example, in an environment that forces a choice between keeping a promise to a supervisor and breaking it to complete the task, a late capabilities-focused o3 checkpoint breaks the promise 87% of the time when SDF documents say the grader rewards task completion, versus 9% when they say it rewards honesty (a choice its chain-of-thought often makes explicit). An earlier checkpoint is far less sensitive (40% vs. 24%). Our method also generalizes to reward-hacking models. A model organism trained to reward-hack (gpt-oss-120b) is more than twice as sensitive to grader preferences as the unmodified model, with the mean behavioral shift in favor of the grader rising from 33% to 86%. These results indicate that RL can increase reward-seeking over the course of training, producing models that may act against their developers’ intentions when they believe that doing so leads to higher reward.</p><p>Learn more at <a href="https://rewardseeking.ai/">rewardseeking.ai</a></p><p>Watch a short explainer video: <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nbyV64ZR2Uk">Measuring Reward Seeking in AI Models (Apollo Research x OpenAI)</a></p><p>Watch the author roundtable: <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n9pNnWYemqM">Is AI doing the right thing for the wrong reasons?</a></p></div></div><div class="paper-left_item desktop-hide"><div class="paper-table_share"><p class="text-size-medium text-color-primary text-weight-medium">Share this article</p><div class="footer_social-link"><a fs-socialshare-element="twitter" href="#" target="_blank" class="social-link w-inline-block"><div class="icon-1x1-medium w-embed">    <div class="social-slot is-first text-color-primary">

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";

  var CONFIG = {
    article:  ".blog-rich-text",      // rich text field with the article body
    // Rich text field holding the [^n]: definitions. May sit inside the article
    // or anywhere else on the page; it gets hidden either way.
    source:   ".paper-right_footnotes, .footnotes-source",
    heading:  "References",
    highlightMs: 1500
  };

  /* Never rewrite [^n] that sits inside these — they are literal text there. */
  var SKIP_TAGS = { CODE: 1, PRE: 1, KBD: 1, SAMP: 1, SCRIPT: 1, STYLE: 1, TEXTAREA: 1, A: 1 };

  var REF_SPLIT = /(\[\^[^\]\s]+\])/g;
  var REF_ONE   = /^\[\^([^\]\s]+)\]$/;
  var DEF_LINE  = /^\[\^([^\]\s]+)\]:\s*([\s\S]+)$/;
  var URL_BARE  = /(https?:\/\/[^\s<]+[^\s<.,;:)\]])/g;

    if (document.readyState === "loading") {
      document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", fn, { once: true });
    } else {

  function centerScroll(target) {
    var top = target.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY
            - window.innerHeight / 2 + target.offsetHeight / 2;

    var walker = document.createTreeWalker(root, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT);
    var nodes = [];

      if (!SKIP_TAGS[walker.currentNode.parentNode.nodeName]) nodes.push(walker.currentNode);

      if (!text || text.indexOf("http") === -1) return;
      var frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
      var last = 0;
      text.replace(URL_BARE, function (url, offset) {
        if (offset > last) frag.appendChild(document.createTextNode(text.slice(last, offset)));

        a.href = url;
        a.target = "_blank";
        a.rel = "noopener noreferrer";
        a.textContent = url;
        frag.appendChild(a);
        last = offset + url.length;
        return url;

     field is absent we fall back to definitions written inside the article,
     which is how the original single-field content was authored.           */

  function collectDefinitions(article) {
    var defs = new Map();

    function harvest(scope, removeNode) {
      scope.querySelectorAll("p, li").forEach(function (el) {
        var m = el.textContent.trim().match(DEF_LINE);
        if (!m) return;
        var id = m[1].trim();
        /* Keep the inline markup (links with anchor text) instead of the
           plain text the naive version used — strip only the "[^n]:" label. */
        var holder = document.createElement("span");
        holder.innerHTML = el.innerHTML;
        stripLabel(holder, id);
        linkifyBareUrls(holder);
        defs.set(id, holder.innerHTML.trim());
        if (removeNode) el.remove();
      });
    }

    var sources = document.querySelectorAll(CONFIG.source);
    sources.forEach(function (source) {
      harvest(source, false);
      source.setAttribute("hidden", "");
      source.style.display = "none";

    var ol = document.createElement("ol");

    defs.forEach(function (content, id) {
      var n = uses.get(id);
      if (!n) return;                       // defined but never referenced

      var li = document.createElement("li");
      li.id = "footnote-" + id;

      var span = document.createElement("span");
      span.className = "footnote-content";

        back.setAttribute("aria-label", "Return to reference " + id);
        li.appendChild(document.createTextNode(" "));
        li.appendChild(back);

      ol.appendChild(li);

    section.appendChild(h);
    section.appendChild(ol);

  }

  ready(function () {
    var article = document.querySelector(CONFIG.article);

    if (article && !article.dataset.footnotesDone) {
      article.dataset.footnotesDone = "1";

      var defs = collectDefinitions(article);

        if (uses.size) article.appendChild(buildSection(defs, uses));

    /* One delegated handler for every same-page anchor: footnote refs,
       backlinks and any table-of-contents link all centre their target. */
    document.addEventListener("click", function (event) {
      var link = event.target.closest('a[href*="#"]');
      if (!link) return;

      var url = new URL(link.href, window.location.href);
      if (url.pathname !== window.location.pathname || !url.hash || url.hash === "#") return;

      var id = decodeURIComponent(url.hash.slice(1));
      var target = document.getElementById(id);
      if (!target) return;

      event.preventDefault();
      event.stopPropagation();
      event.stopImmediatePropagation();

      centerScroll(target);

      var isFootnote = link.closest(".footnote-reference, .footnotes");
      if (isFootnote) {
        document.querySelectorAll(".footnote-highlight").forEach(function (el) {
          el.classList.remove("footnote-highlight");
        });
        var hit = target.closest(".footnote-reference") || target;
        hit.classList.add("footnote-highlight");
        window.setTimeout(function () {
          hit.classList.remove("footnote-highlight");
        }, CONFIG.highlightMs);
        history.replaceState(null, "", url.hash);
      } else {
        history.pushState(null, "", url.hash);
      }

    /* Deep link straight to a footnote: centre it after layout settles. */
    if (window.location.hash) {
      var deep = document.getElementById(decodeURIComponent(window.location.hash.slice(1)));
      if (deep) window.requestAnimationFrame(function () { centerScroll(deep); });
    }
  });
})();

          if (inner) out += '`' + inner + '`';
          break;
        case 'A':
          inner = inline(child).trim();
          var href = absUrl(child, 'href');
          out += href && inner ? '[' + inner + '](' + href + ')' : inner;
          break;
        case 'IMG':
          out += image(child);
          break;
        case 'SUP':
          inner = inline(child).trim();
          if (inner) out += '^' + inner;
          break;
        case 'SUB':
          inner = inline(child).trim();
          if (inner) out += '_' + inner;
          break;
        default:
          out += inline(child);
      }
    });
    return out;
  }
 
  function image(img) {
    var src = absUrl(img, 'src');
    if (!src) return '';
    return '![' + esc(collapse(img.getAttribute('alt') || '')) + '](' + src + ')';
  }
 
  /* ---------- block serialisation ---------- */
 
  function listBlock(el, depth) {
    var ordered = el.tagName === 'OL';
    var start = parseInt(el.getAttribute('start'), 10);
    var index = isNaN(start) ? 1 : start;
    var pad = new Array(depth + 1).join('  ');
    var lines = [];
 
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(el.children, function (li) {
      if (li.tagName !== 'LI' || skip(li)) return;
 
      var marker = ordered ? (index++) + '. ' : '- ';
      var nested = [];
      var text = '';
 
      Array.prototype.forEach.call(li.childNodes, function (child) {
        if (child.nodeType === 1 && (child.tagName === 'UL' || child.tagName === 'OL')) {
          nested.push(listBlock(child, depth + 1));
        } else if (child.nodeType === 1 && BLOCK_TAGS[child.tagName] && child.tagName !== 'LI') {
          nested.push(blocks(child, depth + 1));
        } else if (child.nodeType === 1) {
          text += inline({ childNodes: [child] });
        } else if (child.nodeType === 3) {
          text += esc(collapse(child.nodeValue));
        }
      });
 
      text = text.trim();
      // Continuation lines of a list item must align under the marker.
      var indented = text.replace(/\n/g, '\n' + pad + new Array(marker.length + 1).join(' '));
      lines.push(pad + marker + indented);
      nested.filter(Boolean).forEach(function (n) { lines.push(n); });
    });
 
    return lines.join('\n');
  }
 
  function tableBlock(table) {
    var rows = Array.prototype.slice.call(table.querySelectorAll('tr')).filter(function (tr) {
      return !skip(tr);
    });
    if (!rows.length) return '';
 
    var grid = rows.map(function (tr) {
      return Array.prototype.slice.call(tr.children).map(function (cell) {
        return inline(cell).replace(/\n/g, ' ').replace(/\|/g, '\\|').trim();
      });
    });
 
    var cols = grid.reduce(function (max, r) { return Math.max(max, r.length); }, 0);
    grid.forEach(function (r) { while (r.length < cols) r.push(''); });
 
    // A table with no <th> still needs a header row for valid markdown.
    var hasHead = !!table.querySelector('th');
    var head = hasHead ? grid.shift() : new Array(cols + 1).join('|').split('|').slice(0, cols);
    var sep = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < cols; i++) sep.push('---');
 
    var lines = ['| ' + head.join(' | ') + ' |', '| ' + sep.join(' | ') + ' |'];
    grid.forEach(function (r) { lines.push('| ' + r.join(' | ') + ' |'); });
    return lines.join('\n');
  }
 
  function figureBlock(fig) {
    var img = fig.querySelector('img');
    var cap = fig.querySelector('figcaption');
    var parts = [];
    if (img) parts.push(image(img));
    if (cap) {
      var t = inline(cap).trim();
      if (t) parts.push('*' + t + '*');
    }
    if (!parts.length) parts.push(blocks(fig, 0));
    return parts.filter(Boolean).join('\n\n');
  }
 
  function blocks(root, depth) {
    var out = [];
    var pendingInline = '';
 
    function flush() {
      var t = pendingInline.trim();
      if (t) out.push(t);
      pendingInline = '';
    }
 
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(root.childNodes, function (node) {
      if (node.nodeType === 3) { pendingInline += esc(collapse(node.nodeValue)); return; }
      if (node.nodeType !== 1) return;
      if (skip(node)) return;
 
      var tag = node.tagName;
 
      if (!BLOCK_TAGS[tag]) { pendingInline += inline({ childNodes: [node] }); return; }
      flush();
 
      switch (tag) {
        case 'H1': case 'H2': case 'H3': case 'H4': case 'H5': case 'H6':
          var level = new Array(parseInt(tag.charAt(1), 10) + 1).join('#');
          var htext = inline(node).replace(/\n/g, ' ').trim();
          if (htext) out.push(level + ' ' + htext);
          break;
        case 'HR':
          out.push('---');
          break;
        case 'UL': case 'OL':
          out.push(listBlock(node, 0));
          break;
        case 'TABLE':
          out.push(tableBlock(node));
          break;
        case 'FIGURE':
          out.push(figureBlock(node));
          break;
        case 'PRE':
          var code = node.querySelector('code');
          var lang = '';
          var cls = (code || node).className || '';
          var m = cls.match(/(?:language|lang)-([\w+#-]+)/);
          if (m) lang = m[1];
          out.push('```' + lang + '\n' + (node.textContent || '').replace(/\s+$/, '') + '\n```');
          break;
        case 'BLOCKQUOTE':
          var q = blocks(node, depth);
          if (q) out.push(q.replace(/^/gm, '> '));
          break;
        case 'P': case 'FIGCAPTION': case 'DT': case 'DD':
          var p = inline(node).trim();
          if (p) out.push(p);
          break;
        default:
          // Layout wrapper (div/section/...) — recurse, keep its children as blocks.
          var nestedBlocks = blocks(node, depth);
          if (nestedBlocks) out.push(nestedBlocks);
      }
    });
 
    flush();
    return out.filter(Boolean).join('\n\n');
  }
 
  /* ---------- document assembly ---------- */
 
  function buildMarkdown() {
    var source = document.querySelector(SOURCE_SEL);
    if (!source) return '';
 
    var parts = [];
 
    if (INCLUDE_TITLE) {
      var titleEl = document.querySelector(TITLE_SEL);
      var title = titleEl ? collapse(titleEl.textContent).trim() : collapse(document.title).trim();
      if (title) parts.push('# ' + title);
    }
 
    if (INCLUDE_META) {
      var meta = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll(META_SEL))
        .filter(function (el) { return !isHidden(el); })
        .map(function (el) { return collapse(el.textContent).trim(); })
        .filter(Boolean);
      if (meta.length) parts.push(meta.join(' · '));
    }
 
    if (INCLUDE_URL) parts.push('Source: ' + location.href.split('#')[0]);
 
    if (parts.length) parts.push('---');
    parts.push(blocks(source, 0));
 
    return trimBlank(parts.join('\n\n'));
  }
 
  /* ---------- clipboard ---------- */
 
  function legacyCopy(text) {
    var ta = document.createElement('textarea');
    ta.value = text;
    ta.setAttribute('readonly', '');
    ta.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;top:0;left:-9999px;opacity:0;';
    document.body.appendChild(ta);
    ta.select();
    ta.setSelectionRange(0, text.length);
    var ok = false;
    try { ok = document.execCommand('copy'); } catch (e) { ok = false; }
    document.body.removeChild(ta);
    return ok;
  }
 
  function copyText(text) {
    if (navigator.clipboard && window.isSecureContext) {
      return navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).catch(function () {
        if (legacyCopy(text)) return;
        throw new Error('copy failed');
      });
    }
    return legacyCopy(text) ? Promise.resolve() : Promise.reject(new Error('copy failed'));
  }
 
  /* ---------- button wiring ---------- */
  function getToast(btn) {
    var toast = btn.querySelector(TOAST_SEL);
    if (toast) return toast;
    toast = btn._mdToast;
    if (toast && toast.parentNode === btn) return toast;
 
    toast = document.createElement('span');
    toast.setAttribute('data-copy-md', 'toast');
    toast.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
    btn.appendChild(toast);
    btn._mdToast = toast;
    return toast;
  }
 
  function feedback(btn, message, isError) {
    if (btn._mdTimer) clearTimeout(btn._mdTimer);
 
    var toast = getToast(btn);
    toast.textContent = message;
 
    btn.classList.remove('is-copied', 'is-copy-error');
    btn.classList.add(isError ? 'is-copy-error' : 'is-copied');
    btn.setAttribute('data-copy-md-state', isError ? 'error' : 'copied');
 
    btn._mdTimer = setTimeout(function () {
      btn.classList.remove('is-copied', 'is-copy-error');
      btn.removeAttribute('data-copy-md-state');
    }, RESET_MS);
  }
 
  function init() {
    var buttons = document.querySelectorAll(BUTTON_SEL);
    if (!buttons.length) return;
 
    var source = document.querySelector(SOURCE_SEL);
    if (!source) {
      Array.prototype.forEach.call(buttons, function (b) { b.style.display = 'none'; });
      return;
    }
 
    Array.prototype.forEach.call(buttons, function (btn) {
      if (btn.tagName === 'A' && !btn.getAttribute('href')) btn.setAttribute('href', 'javascript:void(0)');
 
      // Bare text directly inside the button can't be hidden with CSS, so wrap
      // it once. Runs before any GSAP split, and splitting a span works the same.
      Array.prototype.slice.call(btn.childNodes).forEach(function (n) {
        if (n.nodeType !== 3 || !n.nodeValue.trim()) return;
        var span = document.createElement('span');
        span.setAttribute('data-copy-md', 'label');
        span.textContent = n.nodeValue;
        btn.replaceChild(span, n);
      });
 
      btn.setAttribute('role', btn.tagName === 'BUTTON' ? 'button' : btn.getAttribute('role') || 'button');
 
      btn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
        e.preventDefault();
        var md = buildMarkdown();
        if (!md) { feedback(btn, FAILED_TEXT, true); return; }
        copyText(md).then(function () {
          feedback(btn, COPIED_TEXT, false);
        }).catch(function () {
          feedback(btn, FAILED_TEXT, true);
        });
      });
    });
  }
 
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
  else init();
})();

Donor FAQs

Here are the most frequently asked questions from Bold.org® donors.
If you don't see your question here, please visit our Help Center or contact us at donors@bold.org.

Donation Details

Are award contributions tax deductible?

Yes! Donations to Bold.org are made through the Bold Foundation, a 501(c)(3) non-profit, so your contribution is tax-deductible. You'll receive an email with documentation for tax purposes after your donation is processed.

Does Bold.org charge donation fees?

No, we do not charge any fees on donations. Every dollar you contribute goes directly to support students, ensuring 100% of your donation impacts educational expenses.

Where does my donation go?

All donations are managed by the Bold Foundation and directly fund scholarships.

What happens to donations until they're awarded?

Donations that are ready for distribution as scholarship awards are held in cash, while other funds are invested in U.S. Treasury bills. This approach allows us to operate fee-free and ensures 100% of your donation goes to students.

How long does it take for donations to process?

Credit card donations process immediately. ACH donations may take 3-5 business days to complete.

Why are awards funded upfront?

Funding upfront ensures scholarships are fully backed before students apply, guaranteeing the award will be available to recipients.

How will my donation be used?

Your tax-deductible donation goes directly to a deserving recipient based on your scholarship's criteria. Awards are generally applied to tuition or student loans, and we require documentation to confirm appropriate use.

Can I set up recurring donations?

Not yet, but we hope to add this feature soon! Reach out to our team at donors@bold.org if you're interested in making a recurring gift.

Scholarship, Fellowship, and Grant Details

What types of expenses can awards cover?

Awards can cover tuition, student loans, or other educational expenses that enhance a recipient's academic or artistic growth.

How are applications evaluated?

Our Scholarship Evaluation Specialists review each application carefully to ensure alignment with your criteria. Applications undergo a multi-point assessment, scoring various aspects of the student's profile, background, and goals related to the scholarship's purpose. We also evaluate the essay for originality, checking for AI usage and plagiarism to maintain fairness and authenticity.

Can reviewers have multiple logins?

Currently, each donor account supports one login. You can add reviewers to your account by inviting them through the "Team Members" tab.

Can award applications include images or video?

Yes! For more details, see our Award Features page.

Can I interview candidates?

Live or scheduled interviews with applicants aren't possible. However, if seeing or hearing from your candidate is important, you can request a video or audio submission as part of the application.

Can I request letters of recommendation?

Yes, you can request recommendation letters as part of the application. However, please note that we do not validate these materials.

How are no-essay awards reviewed?

No-essay awards are evaluated based on applicants' profiles, which provide detailed information about their backgrounds, goals, and achievements.

Can I share my scholarship with students or schools?

Absolutely! Sharing your scholarship can help attract applicants, especially if the eligibility criteria are specific or narrow.

How does Bold.org promote scholarships?

We promote published scholarships to eligible students within our network to ensure qualified applicants apply.

Scholarship Funds

What is the process for getting a fund live?

To create a fund, sign up as a donor, then submit your fund goal through your donor dashboard. Our team will work closely with you to launch it within 2-3 days. For more details, review our guide on How to Propose a Scholarship or Fund.

What is the difference between a fund and a scholarship?

A fund is a fundraising page, while a scholarship is where students apply. You can have either individually or both together. The fund outlines your mission and goal amount, while the scholarship includes applicant criteria and background. Students apply through the scholarship page, not the fund page.

How do I publish a scholarship after I raise money through the fund?

Once your goal is met, transfer the funds to your scholarship proposal in your dashboard. Click "review proposal," then "fund the scholarship," and select your fund as the payment method. For directions, review our guide on How to Fund & Publish Your Scholarship.

Will the fundraiser automatically publish a scholarship once I reach my goal?

No, you'll need to create a scholarship draft first and manually fund it through your dashboard once your goal is met. For more details, review our guide on How to Propose a Scholarship or Fund.

Can I remove the funds from the account and transfer them to a personal account at any point in time?

No, all funds must support scholarships on Bold.org.

Will the money in the fundraiser gain interest over time?

No, donations made to scholarship funds do not accrue interest.

Applicant Details

How many applications to my scholarship should I expect?

Application numbers depend on the award's criteria and timeline. Scholarships with narrow criteria typically receive 50-200 applications, while broader scholarships can receive hundreds.

What types of applicants are on Bold.org?

Our student users range from high school students to recent graduates and those repaying student debt or pursuing advanced degrees. We connect eligible applicants to the scholarship based on the award criteria to ensure quality candidates apply.

Is Bold.org open to non-students?

Yes! Many of our members are graduates focused on paying off student debt.

How are scholarship recipients notified?

Recipients are notified directly through our platform on the announcement date. We send them a congratulatory message and immediately begin verifying their eligibility to ensure prompt award distribution.

What if I want to change my scholarship selection criteria after launch?

Criteria cannot be narrowed after launch but can be expanded if you're seeking a larger applicant pool.

What are Bold Points?

Bold Points are awarded to students for actively engaging on the platform, such as by completing their profiles thoroughly and applying to scholarships. These points help students stand out and demonstrate their commitment to personal and academic growth.

How does Bold support students going through the application process?

Our support team is available at contact@bold.org to assist students throughout the application process.

Bold.org Details

What is Bold.org's mission?

Our mission is to eliminate student debt by empowering students to access education affordably and sustainably. We provide funding opportunities and raise awareness about financial resources, including scholarships and grants. Bold.org aims to inspire a lifelong commitment to learning and growth, fostering collective progress for society.

What is the Bold Foundation?

The Bold Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that works closely with Bold.org to ensure that all donations are tax-deductible and go directly toward funding scholarships. Through this partnership, we handle every step of the scholarship process—from proposal evaluation and donor onboarding to scholarship management and award distribution—ensuring that 100% of each donation reaches students without any administrative deductions.

What types of donors are on Bold.org?

Our donors include individuals, families, businesses of all sizes, foundations, and more. We make it simple for anyone to create and manage customized scholarships, fellowships, and grants in just minutes.

How can I contact Bold.org for support?

You can reach us directly at donors@bold.org. For more information, please refer to our guide on contacting the Bold.org Donor Team.

Scholarship form

Please complete all fields and make sure you provide the documentation listed in the final section of this form. Please ensure each page is clearly named and numbered.

Applications for 2027 opened on Monday, 5 October 2026 at 9:00am and close on Friday, 20 November at 5:00pm.

Personal Details
Address Validation
How did you find out about the FMG Agriculture Scholarship?
Education
University
University Please select the university you will be attending
Have you applied/received (or do you intend to apply) for any other tertiary study scholarships?
Work experience

Please fill out your work experience details to include Year, Job title/description, Company/Farm/Manager, Key Responsibilities

Essays


Please attach all the below answers in one document and label it "FirstNameLastName_answers"

About Me

Tell us about yourself, including what your personal interests and future agricultural aspirations are, as well as your involvement in the agriculture industry [500 words].

Achievements

Tell us what your proudest achievements are including any academic, sporting, cultural, agricultural and leadership/awards recognition [500 words].

Industry Essay

Identify an issue, challenge or opportunity relevant to one of the primary industries and explain how the industry can overcome or take advantage of it. [500 words]

To accompany your application, please provide the following documents:

  1. Fill out the Personal Details, Work Experience, and Education sections. Attach the About Me, Achievements and Industry Essay sections, in one document labelled "FirstNameLastName_answers"
  2. Attach a certified copy of your academic results to date, labelled "FirstNameLastName_results"
  3. Attach a copy of the picture page of your New Zealand Passport. If you do not have a New Zealand passport please attach a certified copy of your New Zealand birth certificate or New Zealand Residency Visa, labelled "FirstNameLastName_ID"
  4. Attach a reference and label as "FirstNameLastName_reference"
  5. Read the FMG Agriculture Scholarship Terms and Conditions
  6. If you need help with your application please Email Us

  // Function to convert a select to searchable input
  function makeSearchable(selectId, placeholder) {
    var select = document.getElementById(selectId);
    if (!select) return;
    
    // Hide the original select
    select.style.display = 'none';
    
    // Create search input
    var input = document.createElement('input');
    input.type = 'text';
    input.placeholder = placeholder;
    input.style.cssText = 'width:100%;padding:.375rem .75rem;font-size:1rem;line-height:1.5;color:#495057;background-color:#fff;border:1px solid #3E3939;border-radius:0;box-sizing:border-box;';
    
    // Create dropdown list
    var dropdown = document.createElement('div');
    dropdown.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;z-index:9999;background:#fff;border:1px solid #3E3939;max-height:200px;overflow-y:auto;width:100%;display:none;';
    
    // Get all options
    var options = Array.from(select.options).filter(function(o) { return o.value !== ''; });
    
    function showOptions(filter) {
      dropdown.innerHTML = '';
      var filtered = options.filter(function(o) {
        return o.text.toLowerCase().indexOf(filter.toLowerCase()) !== -1;
      });
      if (filtered.length === 0) {
        dropdown.style.display = 'none';
        return;
      }
      filtered.forEach(function(o) {
        var item = document.createElement('div');
        item.textContent = o.text;
        item.style.cssText = 'padding:6px 10px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;';
        item.addEventListener('mouseover', function() { item.style.background = '#f0f0f0'; });
        item.addEventListener('mouseout', function() { item.style.background = '#fff'; });
        item.addEventListener('click', function() {
          select.value = o.value;
          input.value = o.text;
          dropdown.style.display = 'none';
        });
        dropdown.appendChild(item);
      });
      dropdown.style.display = 'block';
    }
    
    input.addEventListener('input', function() {
      if (input.value.length > 0) {
        showOptions(input.value);
      } else {
        select.value = '';
        dropdown.style.display = 'none';
      }
    });
    
    input.addEventListener('focus', function() {
      if (input.value.length > 0) showOptions(input.value);
    });
    
    document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
      if (e.target !== input) dropdown.style.display = 'none';
    });
    
    // Wrap in relative div
    var wrapper = document.createElement('div');
    wrapper.style.position = 'relative';
    select.parentNode.insertBefore(wrapper, select);
    wrapper.appendChild(input);
    wrapper.appendChild(dropdown);
    wrapper.appendChild(select);
  }

            <h1><span style="color: #8f3f3f;">The Hagan Scholarships</span></h1>
<p>The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship, providing recipients with the opportunity to achieve their goals and graduate from college debt-free. Parents’ Adjusted Household Income must not exceed $125,000. The scholarship provides $1,000 to help purchase essential items for college and up to $7,500 each semester for up to 8 consecutive semesters. Free workshops, free Schwab Brokerage Accounts, and free Study Abroad opportunities provide recipients with a practical understanding of important life skills not typically covered in the school curriculum. Hagan Scholars have attended 745 colleges and universities located in all 50 states and the District of Columbia and have studied abroad in 64 countries.</p>
<p>The Hagan Graduate Scholarships are for Hagan Scholars who have graduated from college while enrolled in the Hagan Scholarship Program and are good for up to four additional consecutive semesters, providing up to $7,500 each semester to attend graduate school or the first two years of a professional program.</p>
<p>The Hagan International Graduate Scholarships follow the same terms as the Hagan Graduate Scholarships. International applicants must have graduated or will graduate from a foreign institution, and must have received an acceptance letter for the upcoming fall semester as a first-time graduate student at a college or university located in the U.S.</p>

  // Only run on Portal Search page
  var form = document.getElementById('form_959');
  if (!form) return;

  // Function to convert a select to searchable input
  function makeSearchable(selectId, placeholder) {
    var select = document.getElementById(selectId);
    if (!select) return;
    
    // Hide the original select
    select.style.display = 'none';
    
    // Create search input
    var input = document.createElement('input');
    input.type = 'text';
    input.placeholder = placeholder;
    input.style.cssText = 'width:100%;padding:.375rem .75rem;font-size:1rem;line-height:1.5;color:#495057;background-color:#fff;border:1px solid #3E3939;border-radius:0;box-sizing:border-box;';
    
    // Create dropdown list
    var dropdown = document.createElement('div');
    dropdown.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;z-index:9999;background:#fff;border:1px solid #3E3939;max-height:200px;overflow-y:auto;width:100%;display:none;';
    
    // Get all options
    var options = Array.from(select.options).filter(function(o) { return o.value !== ''; });
    
    function showOptions(filter) {
      dropdown.innerHTML = '';
      var filtered = options.filter(function(o) {
        return o.text.toLowerCase().indexOf(filter.toLowerCase()) !== -1;
      });
      if (filtered.length === 0) {
        dropdown.style.display = 'none';
        return;
      }
      filtered.forEach(function(o) {
        var item = document.createElement('div');
        item.textContent = o.text;
        item.style.cssText = 'padding:6px 10px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;';
        item.addEventListener('mouseover', function() { item.style.background = '#f0f0f0'; });
        item.addEventListener('mouseout', function() { item.style.background = '#fff'; });
        item.addEventListener('click', function() {
          select.value = o.value;
          input.value = o.text;
          dropdown.style.display = 'none';
        });
        dropdown.appendChild(item);
      });
      dropdown.style.display = 'block';
    }
    
    input.addEventListener('input', function() {
      if (input.value.length > 0) {
        showOptions(input.value);
      } else {
        select.value = '';
        dropdown.style.display = 'none';
      }
    });
    
    input.addEventListener('focus', function() {
      if (input.value.length > 0) showOptions(input.value);
    });
    
    document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
      if (e.target !== input) dropdown.style.display = 'none';
    });
    
    // Wrap in relative div
    var wrapper = document.createElement('div');
    wrapper.style.position = 'relative';
    select.parentNode.insertBefore(wrapper, select);
    wrapper.appendChild(input);
    wrapper.appendChild(dropdown);
    wrapper.appendChild(select);
  }

  // Only run on Portal Search page
  var form = document.getElementById('form_959');
  if (!form) return;

  // Function to convert a select to searchable input
  function makeSearchable(selectId, placeholder) {
    var select = document.getElementById(selectId);
    if (!select) return;
    
    // Hide the original select
    select.style.display = 'none';
    
    // Create search input
    var input = document.createElement('input');
    input.type = 'text';
    input.placeholder = placeholder;
    input.style.cssText = 'width:100%;padding:.375rem .75rem;font-size:1rem;line-height:1.5;color:#495057;background-color:#fff;border:1px solid #3E3939;border-radius:0;box-sizing:border-box;';
    
    // Create dropdown list
    var dropdown = document.createElement('div');
    dropdown.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;z-index:9999;background:#fff;border:1px solid #3E3939;max-height:200px;overflow-y:auto;width:100%;display:none;';
    
    // Get all options
    var options = Array.from(select.options).filter(function(o) { return o.value !== ''; });
    
    function showOptions(filter) {
      dropdown.innerHTML = '';
      var filtered = options.filter(function(o) {
        return o.text.toLowerCase().indexOf(filter.toLowerCase()) !== -1;
      });
      if (filtered.length === 0) {
        dropdown.style.display = 'none';
        return;
      }
      filtered.forEach(function(o) {
        var item = document.createElement('div');
        item.textContent = o.text;
        item.style.cssText = 'padding:6px 10px;cursor:pointer;font-size:14px;';
        item.addEventListener('mouseover', function() { item.style.background = '#f0f0f0'; });
        item.addEventListener('mouseout', function() { item.style.background = '#fff'; });
        item.addEventListener('click', function() {
          select.value = o.value;
          input.value = o.text;
          dropdown.style.display = 'none';
        });
        dropdown.appendChild(item);
      });
      dropdown.style.display = 'block';
    }
    
    input.addEventListener('input', function() {
      if (input.value.length > 0) {
        showOptions(input.value);
      } else {
        select.value = '';
        dropdown.style.display = 'none';
      }
    });
    
    input.addEventListener('focus', function() {
      if (input.value.length > 0) showOptions(input.value);
    });
    
    document.addEventListener('click', function(e) {
      if (e.target !== input) dropdown.style.display = 'none';
    });
    
    // Wrap in relative div
    var wrapper = document.createElement('div');
    wrapper.style.position = 'relative';
    select.parentNode.insertBefore(wrapper, select);
    wrapper.appendChild(input);
    wrapper.appendChild(dropdown);
    wrapper.appendChild(select);
  }

 makeSearchable('field_4', 'By name or state');

            <h1><span style="color: #8f3f3f;">Hagan Scholarship Fall Application<br />For the 2027-2028 Academic Year </span></h1>
<p><strong>Before Applying</strong> — The Hagan Scholarship has specific requirements that must be maintained every semester to keep the scholarship. Please review the <a href="https://haganscholarships.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/3-Scholarship_Particulars_83126-su3.pdf">Scholarship Particulars </a>before applying, so you will understand what is expected of you if awarded a scholarship. We communicate with applicants only to avoid miscommunication.</p>
<p><strong><a href="https://fs28.formsite.com/DanHagan/zamqld4dle/signup">Hagan Scholarship Application</a>  </strong><br />1. For students in the 2027 high school graduating class.<br />2. Applicants can apply one time only.<br />3. Click on the Above Link, then create a Username and Password to access the Application.<br />4. Up to 1,500 Hagan Scholarships can be awarded for the 2027-2028 academic year.<br />5. Updates are posted on the <a href="https://haganscholarships.org/timeline/">Application Timeline Link</a>.<br /><strong>6. Application Deadline: December 1, 2026.</strong></p>
<p><strong>Resources<br /></strong>1. <a href="https://haganscholarships.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/10-2-26-FALL-Website-HSF-U.S.-BROCHURE-su3.pdf">Hagan Scholarship Brochure</a> — An overview of the scholarship, eligibility, responsibilities and benefits.<br />2. <a href="https://haganscholarships.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/HSF-U.S.-Application-Tips-10-2-26-su3-.pdf">Tips on How to Prepare a Successful Application</a></p>
<p><strong>Eligibility Criteria. No Exceptions.<br /></strong>1. Must attend a high school located in the United States.<br />2. Eligible high schools include public, private, charter, magnet, and STEM schools.<br />3. Must be in the high school graduating class.<br />4. All students who meet the eligibility criteria can apply regardless of citizenship.<br />5. Must have achieved a 3.50 CGPA, be goal-driven, and willing to work to achieve their goals.<br />6. Must provide a current copy of the applicant’s High School Transcript.<br />7. Must provide an “unsealed” Letter of Recommendation.<br />8. Must enroll in an eligible four-year College or University the first fall semester following high school graduation.<br />9. The scholarship cannot be used to attend a community college, junior college, or online institution.<br />10. Must maintain a four-year graduation schedule, or complete the equivalent within four years if enrolled in a professional program.<br />11. Must work 240 hours from January 1, 2027 until September 1, 2027 to be eligible for a fall semester disbursement. Work must be regularly scheduled non-family employment performed under supervision for compensation. Employment can be full-time or part-time.<br />12. Parents’ Adjusted Gross Household Income reported for 2025 Federal Income Tax Purposes must not have exceeded $125,000.<br />13. U.S. Citizens selected as Finalists must provide the first two pages of their FAFSA Summary. The FAFSA Summary must show the SAI.<br />14. Non-U.S. Citizens selected as Finalists must provide Proof of non-U.S. Citizenship. Copy of Foreign Passport or Green Card.<br />15. Must apply for Federal and State grants if eligible.</p>
<p>The Hagan Scholarship is a hand-up, not a hand-out. It is earned each semester by meeting the scholarship criteria. The intended recipients are high-achieving, goal-driven students who have financial need.</p>
<p>“You can’t go back and change the beginning, but you can start where you are and change the ending.”<br /><em>C.S. Lewis</em></p>
<p><em>Decisions made by HSF are final and not subject to appeal. Terms and Conditions are subject to change without notice.</em></p>

About IISER Kolkata

Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Kolkata (IISER Kolkata) was established in 2006 by the Ministry of Human Resource Development (now Ministry of Education), Government of India. IISER Kolkata is designed to reach the prestigious position in the global setting that IISc, IIMs and IITs presently enjoy. IISER Kolkata is an autonomous institution awarding its own degrees. The central theme of the IISER Kolkata is to integrate education with research so that undergraduate teaching as well as doctoral and postdoctoral research work could be carried out in basic sciences.

Smart Materials, Methods and Applications (SMMA) 2026

SMMA 2026 aims to bring together leading faculty members, researchers, and students working across the broad areas of Materials Science to exchange recent scientific advances, foster interdisciplinary discussions, and promote new research collaborations. The conference will feature invited lectures by eminent scientists, along with poster presentations showcasing the work of student researchers. Participants will have the opportunity to explore emerging ideas, share perspectives, and build connections across diverse areas of materials research.

Date 03-05 December 2026
Venue Asima Chatterjee, IISER Kolkata
Register View Speakers

About the Symposium

Interdisciplinary conversations for next-generation functional materials

The symposium is designed for meaningful interaction among faculty, postdoctoral researchers, students and visiting scientists, with a focus on research exchange across chemical, biological and physical sciences.

SMMA 2026 is envisioned as a vibrant forum for scientists, academicians, researchers, and young scholars to share ideas and explore emerging directions in materials science. The conference will span diverse and interconnected themes, including Soft Matter, Biomaterials, Functional Materials, Energy, and Catalysis, providing an opportunity to highlight recent breakthroughs and evolving research paradigms. Through a series of invited lectures by distinguished experts, complemented by poster sessions featuring contributions from students and early-career researchers, SMMA 2026 seeks to encourage meaningful scientific dialogue, strengthen interdisciplinary connections, and catalyse new collaborations across fields.

About The Hosts

Centre for Advanced Functional Materials

The Centre for Advanced Functional Materials (CAFM) at IISER Kolkata serves as a multidisciplinary platform for advancing research and education in the rapidly evolving field of materials science. The Centre brings together researchers with diverse expertise to address fundamental scientific questions and develop materials with tailored structures, properties, and functionalities. By encouraging close interaction among chemists, physicists, biologists, materials scientists, and engineers, CAFM provides an environment in which ideas can move seamlessly from molecular and nanoscale design to functional systems and practical applications.

Through its interdisciplinary research ecosystem, CAFM seeks to bridge the gap between fundamental materials discovery and technological innovation. The Centre promotes collaborative projects, knowledge exchange, advanced training, and the development of young researchers equipped to tackle complex scientific challenges. In this spirit, CAFM provides an ideal academic environment for bringing together researchers from complementary disciplines and fostering new scientific partnerships. Its broad research portfolio reflects the increasingly interconnected nature of modern materials science, where advances at the molecular, nanoscale, and macroscopic levels collectively enable transformative technologies.

IISER Kolkata

Established in 2006, the Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Kolkata (IISER Kolkata) is a premier institution dedicated to advancing excellence in science education, fundamental research, and interdisciplinary scholarship. As one of the IISERs established by the Government of India, the Institute was founded with the vision of creating an academic environment where rigorous scientific education is closely integrated with cutting-edge research.

IISER Kolkata follows a research-driven model of education in which students are encouraged to engage with contemporary scientific questions from the early stages of their academic journey. The Institute offers a range of programmes, including the BS-MS dual degree, MS, Integrated PhD, PhD, and postdoctoral programmes, providing opportunities for students and researchers to pursue advanced training across diverse areas of the basic sciences. By bringing together education, fundamental research, advanced training, and interdisciplinary collaboration, IISER Kolkata seeks to nurture the next generation of scientists and contribute to the advancement of knowledge at both national and international levels. The Institute continues to build a dynamic academic community in which curiosity-driven research, scientific innovation, and excellence in education are mutually reinforcing.

MATS general application process

MATS supports researchers and field-builders across seven tracks: Empirical, Theory, Strategy & Forecasting, Policy & Governance, Systems Security, Founding & Field-Building, and Biosecurity. You can apply to one or more of these tracks in the Stage 1 application.

Getting into MATS
Learn more:
Tracks

Stage 1: General application (closed September 6th)

The general application asks for:

  • Your background
  • Short responses (some general, some track specific)
  • Contact details for two references (we won't reach out to them until later in the process)

Returning applicants from previous 2026 application rounds can sign in to pre-fill their application.

For more on what we and mentors are looking for, see getting into MATS.

Stage 2: Central evaluations (September)

If you advance past Stage 1, you’ll complete additional evaluations before your application is reviewed by mentors. The process differs by track.

For Empirical, Stage 2 has two phases:

  1. Empirical assessments: You’ll complete one or two standardized assessments evaluating research taste and technical implementation skills.
  2. Stream selection: If you advance, you’ll apply to and rank the specific research streams you’d like to join.

For all other tracks, you’ll proceed directly to stream selection.

Each track contains multiple streams, each led by one or more mentors with a shared research agenda. When applying to streams, you’ll answer stream-specific questions. These are usually short responses, though some streams may ask for a longer research proposal.

Stage 3: Mentor review (October to early November)

Mentors review applications to their streams and rank the applicants they’d like to work with. Mentors often invite applicants to complete interviews and work tests during this stage.

A final matching process uses both mentor and applicant rankings to determine offers.

Offers (Early to mid-November)

Final offers are sent in early to mid-November. The program begins January 19, 2027.

Frequently Asked Questions

When will I hear about my application status?

We will contact all applicants who get into stage 2 with details on how to use the applicant dashboard, which you can use to check the status of your application.

When will my references be contacted?

We contact references only for select candidates in Stage 2. You'll provide your referees' names when you apply, but they won't receive anything from us unless your application progresses.

What do the assessments involve, and how long will the application take?

Plan to set aside a few hours for the initial application — more if you're applying to several tracks. You can expect two long-form answers (about 200-600 words each) and a 20-minute reasoning test, plus one to three track-specific questions for tracks requiring question responses. The reasoning test covers numerical literacy, probabilistic reasoning, and spatial reasoning; no specialized preparation is needed.

If you advance to the empirical work test, the coding assessment takes 3–5 hours. Stage 3 interviews and work tests from mentors vary by stream.

If I'm not accepted, can I reapply to a future cohort?

Yes, and we encourage it. Applying to a previous cohort doesn't count against you, and we routinely have candidates who are accepted after applying numerous times.

	<div class="container">
		<h1 class="h2">AI Economy Institute (AIEI) Program</h1>

		<div class="row mt-4">
			<div class="col-12 col-md-9">
				<div class="publication-citation small">
					

	<p class="m-0"><time datetime="2025-08-01">August 2025</time></p>


				</div>
			</div>
					</div>
		<div class="row mt-5 mb-4 mb-md-5">
			<div class="col-12 col-md-9">
				<div class="pr-md-4">
					
					<div class="excerpt">
						


<img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="alignnone size-medium wp-image-1144013" src="https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-300x169.jpg" alt="AI Economy Institute | abstract background" width="300" height="169" srcset="https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-300x169.jpg 300w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-1024x576.jpg 1024w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-768x432.jpg 768w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-1066x600.jpg 1066w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-655x368.jpg 655w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-240x135.jpg 240w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-640x360.jpg 640w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-960x540.jpg 960w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1-1280x720.jpg 1280w, https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/AIEI-hero-image_test-1.jpg 1400w" sizes="(max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px" />



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong><em>“Education in the AI Economy: Diffusion, disruption, and design for purposeful transformation”</em></strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The Microsoft AI Economy Institute (AIEI) invites proposals for its second global research call, inviting submissions that will help shape the future of work, learning, and opportunity in the age of generative AI. As GenAI is demonstrating the potential to become the most widely adopted technology in history, we face a defining moment: will its benefits be broadly shared, or will barriers—technical, institutional, regulatory, economic, educational, and cultural—limit its promise for people and communities around the world?</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Microsoft established AIEI to support the diffusion of AI so that it is intentional, inclusive, and informed by rigorous research and scholarly discourse so that societies everywhere may adapt to the economic and social changes AI brings. We seek to accelerate understanding of how GenAI is transforming productivity, labor markets, and workforce development across sectors and geographies. We are especially interested in research that identifies the drivers and barriers to GenAI adoption, and that offers actionable insights for policymakers, educators, employers, and workers.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We invite proposals that address any of the following questions and themes:</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>1.</strong> <strong>The Impact of AI on Entry-Level Jobs</strong></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>What empirical data can be developed to document and analyze the actual impact of AI on entry-level jobs?</li>
<li>In which fields is this impact most pronounced, and why?</li>
<li>How are employers and employees responding? Are employers changing the nature of entry-level work or the employment experience? Are training programs evolving?</li>
<li>How are employees adapting, and what is the impact on AI skills development for both employees and employers?</li>
<li>What lessons can be drawn from apprenticeship programs in Switzerland, Germany, and labor unions?</li>
<li>What does the impact of AI on entry-level jobs mean for the architecture of a career path, including consideration of rapid credentialing and stackable certificates in driving entry-level supply?</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>2. AI and the Impact on K-12 Teaching</strong></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>How is AI likely to impact different aspects of teachers’ work, such as administrative tasks, lesson planning, and grading? And how might this affect teacher retention?</li>
<li>What studies best document how teachers currently spend their time, and how might AI help align this with how they would like to spend their time?</li>
<li>What best practices are emerging, and what will be the impact of AI on classroom time?</li>
<li>What insights can inform the development of new products and tools to support teachers?</li>
<li>What are ethical concerns for use of AI in the K-12 classroom and how are AI ethics taught in a K-12 environment?</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>3. AI and Opportunities for Community, Technical, and Vocational Colleges</strong></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>How do the questions above apply to community colleges and technical/vocational education?</li>
<li>What unique opportunities and challenges exist for these institutions in preparing students for an AI-enabled workforce?</li>
<li>Thinking about the American investment in land-grant institutions, how could the existing two-year, community, and technical colleges network provide a platform for the rapid diffusion of AI fluency into the workforce?</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>4. AI and National Diffusion Differences</strong></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>What conditions best explain why some countries adopt AI faster than others? Do we see links between AI fluency skilling efforts or initiatives and rates of diffusion?</li>
<li>How do national strategies and approaches to data governance and AI regulation shape AI development and use? For example, what strategies are Singapore and the UAE deploying to become early leaders, and are they seeing measurable national dividends?</li>
<li>What policies or practices can be replicated to accelerate responsible AI adoption? How do differences in workforce skills, demographics, and labor needs affect AI adoption across countries?</li>
<li>What policies or programs have helped countries adopt AI responsibly and can they be adapted or scaled elsewhere?</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Research Priorities</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Proposals should provide a unique approach to advancing the AIEI mission of helping society prepare for the economic transformation driven by the advent of GenAI with consideration of what are barriers to GenAI diffusion across sectors and strategies to address such barriers.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><span data-teams="true">AIEI prioritizes proposals that:</span></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>are cross, multi, and interdisciplinary;</li>
<li>consider multilayer impacts of the AI Economy;</li>
<li>propose a novel direction of scholarship in alignment with the AIEI mission;</li>
<li>use existing data sets or leverage existing platforms for collecting data;</li>
<li>consider longer-term effects of AI on education, including both challenges and opportunities; and/or</li>
<li>compare and contrast country and/or regional perspectives.</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Commitment to Program Deliverables</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Each awardee will be expected to:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>Participate in biweekly virtual convenings that may include interim deliverables, including data analyses, initial findings, and working papers (November 1, 2025 – March 31, 2026)</li>
<li>Workshop with other awardees and Microsoft leadership in person at a Microsoft location, providing an abstract, problem and motivation, brief literature review, methodology, preliminary results, discussion, limitations, and references to further scholarship of AIEI (April 2026))</li>
<li>Contribute a book chapter for a book that will synthesize the findings and observations of the research cohort (May 1, 2026)</li>
<li>Participate in a policy workshop (June 2026)</li>
<li>Conduct research and submit a manuscript to a high-quality, open-access journal within nine-months of notification of award (June 30, 2026)</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Researchers will be recognized as senior fellows of the AI Economy Institute and, as appropriate, will be offered opportunities to present their findings at industry events and conferences.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Potential for Long-Term Collaboration</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Collaboration may extend beyond the funding period. Depending on the structure of the AIEI, future opportunities could include:</p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>Additional research projects or commissioned studies and funding focused on AI and the economic impacts thereof;</li>
<li>Consulting engagements, guest lectures, and involvement with industry;</li>
<li>Opportunities to highlight an existing body of work and academic affiliations.</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Eligibility and Format</strong></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>Open to researchers affiliated with accredited universities or research institutions, worldwide</li>
<li>One principal investigator (PI) per proposal; interdisciplinary teams encouraged</li>
<li>Each selected PI will receive a \(75,000 grant plus a travel allowance for the in-person convening; for the travel allowance, awardees in the United States, Canada, and Mexico will receive \)7,500 and all other awardees will receive $20,000</li>
<li>Researchers will produce:
<ul>
<li>A peer-reviewed journal article</li>
<li>A book chapter for AIEI’s second volume, to be published in 2026</li>
</ul>
</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Timeline</strong></p>



<ul class="wp-block-list"><li><strong>Proposal deadline:</strong> September 29, 2025, 5PM Pacific time</li>
<li><strong>Award notification:</strong> October 27, 2025</li>
<li><strong>Research period:</strong> November 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026</li>
<li><strong>Virtual convenings:</strong>  Biweekly, November 1, 2025 – March 31, 2026</li>
<li><strong>Timeline for book chapter deliverables shared:</strong>  November 3-7, 2025</li>
<li><strong>In-person workshop:</strong> April 2026</li>
<li><strong>Book chapter submission:</strong> May 1, 2026</li>
<li><strong>In-person policy convening:</strong> June 2026</li>
<li><strong>Manuscript submission: </strong>June 30, 2026</li></ul>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Review Criteria  </strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The standardized evaluation form will reflect these priorities across five criteria, grading proposals on a 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent) scale across the following 5 criteria:</p>



<ol class="wp-block-list"><li>Scientific merit (20%)– will the project results substantially contribute to the literature?<strong> </strong></li>
<li>Relevance to AIEI (20%) – how well does the project align with the AIEI mission?<strong> </strong></li>
<li>Scientific methodology (20%) – is the methodology sound?<strong> </strong></li>
<li>Scientific feasibility (20%) – can the project be completed within 6 months?<strong> </strong></li>
<li>PI productivity (20%) – does a review of the PI’s bio-sketch suggest that they can complete the project and have it published in a high-quality journal. </li></ol>
