OIST Research Internship Program Description

OIST Research Internship Program

The OIST Graduate School offers education and research opportunities through our Research Internship Program in STEM fields.

Program Description

The research internship program at OIST is a short-term placement of 4-6 months in a laboratory of their choice given the suitability of the intended research, academic background, available funding, and available space in the desired host unit.  

Students may choose their short-term research project from a diverse range of research fields, such as physics, chemistry, mathematical and computational sciences, marine sciences, neuroscience, molecular, cellular, and developmental biology, environmental and ecological science and quantum science.  

For details about the application process and deadlines, please see the section "Apply to Research Internship."


For What Kind of Students is the Research Internship Ideal? 

Students who would like to top up their current research by learning a specific technique will benefit from access to our cutting-edge research equipment and supervision from our world class faculty members.   

As OIST actively fosters and supports interdisciplinary research, the research internship is a great opportunity for students who would like to explore a different research field or would like to add an interdisciplinary approach to their current research interest. 

With more than 1,100 employees from more than 70 countries and territories, the study environment at OIST is highly internationalized and students who are eager to expand their international academic network will benefit from forming connections with people from all over the world early in their academic career. 

For students who value diversity, equity, and inclusion as OIST strives to create and maintain an inclusive, equitable, and diverse environment that does not discriminate against gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, mental or physical disability, medical condition, race, ethnicity, ancestry, culture, national origin, religion, or marital status. Applications from women and other underrepresented groups are strongly encouraged. 
For more details, please refer to the OIST Graduate School Three Policies. 


For Students Considering Applying to OIST’s PhD Program After Their Research Internship 

The research internship is also ideal for students who are considering applying to the PhD program at OIST and would like to use the internship period to find out, whether the study environment at OIST aligns with their research interests and personal preferences. 

Lab Rotation Equivalency 

To those aiming to enroll in the OIST PhD Program within 1 year of finishing the internship, the internship may suffice as one of the PhD Program's required lab rotations. Three lab rotations, including one out of field, will be conducted in your PhD journey here. Research experience as a research intern at OIST may be considered as one in-field lab rotation upon completion of the assignments required for a lab rotation. 
Research interns with an internship of four months or longer are eligible to request this Lab Rotation Equivalency opportunity provided you applied for lab rotation equivalency at the start of the internship and meet the assessment criteria. 
For more details, please refer to the following policy - 4.3.3 Lab Rotations. 

 

Support

The following support is only available for the research intern and does not extend to dependents, family members, or others.

Travel Expenses
One direct round-trip air ticket (travel date will be closest date to the term of placement)

Accommodation
Furnished accommodation on or off campus, funded by OIST or the research unit

Administrative Support
Acquisition of Certificate of Eligibility (CoE) for your visa application and as well as registration procedures

Internship Allowance
2,400 JPY per working day

Transportation Support
OIST Shuttle Bus Pass

What is the application process like?

Our recruitment process typically follows these steps:

  1. Application Submission
    Please submit all required documents as specified in the job posting.
  2. Document Screening
    We will review your application materials. Candidates who pass this stage will be contacted regarding the next steps.
  3. Interviews (may be conducted in multiple rounds)
    Interviews will be held either in person or online. Depending on the position, you may be asked to complete a skills test.
  4. Final Evaluation & Reference Check
    Final candidates may be asked to provide references.
  5. Offer Notification
    Successful candidates will receive an official offer.

*Please note that the selection process may vary depending on the position.

Can I apply for multiple positions at the same time?

You may apply for multiple positions; however, please note that we do not conduct the selection process for multiple applications simultaneously. Applications are reviewed in the order they are received.

Is there an application deadline for each position?

Some positions may have an application deadline, while others will remain open until filled.

Will I be notified if I am not selected?

No. We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Can I reapply if I was not selected previously?

Yes, you are welcome to reapply for other future opportunities. We encourage applicants to continue exploring roles that match their skills and experience, even if they were not selected in a previous application.

What documents do I need to apply for an open position?

The required documents for each position vary. Please refer to the job posting for details.

Do I need to submit recommendation letters or references?

Depending on the position, we may ask you to provide references during the final stages of the hiring process.

Are there any research unit positions?

Yes. Please apply directly through each research unit’s career page.

How can I apply for a faculty position?

Open faculty positions will be listed under "Open Positions" on the Careers Page. Please subscribe to the OIST Mailing List to receive up-to-date opportunities. For inquiries related to faculty hiring, please contact: faculty-recruiting@oist.jp

play a critical role in advancing gender equality, protecting human rights, and challenging systems that perpetuate discrimination and gender-based violence. However, many of these organizations face significant financial and operational challenges that limit their ability to scale their impact and sustain their advocacy efforts.</p>
<p>To address these challenges, <strong>Feminist Opportunities Now (FON)</strong> has emerged as a transformative initiative dedicated to empowering feminist movements globally. Through funding, capacity strengthening, networking opportunities, and movement-building support, FON is helping feminist organizations build resilience, foster inclusivity, and create lasting social change.</p>
<p>Organizations committed to advancing gender justice, eliminating gender-based violence, and promoting equality now have an opportunity to engage with a platform designed specifically to amplify feminist voices and strengthen feminist leadership worldwide.</p>
<h2>About Feminist Opportunities Now (FON)</h2>
<p>Feminist Opportunities Now (FON) is a global initiative focused on supporting feminist movements and organizations that are working tirelessly to create a more equitable and inclusive world.</p>
<p>The initiative is built around three core principles:</p>
<ul>
<li>Empowering feminist organizations</li>
<li>Elevating marginalized voices</li>
<li>Advocating for sustainable gender justice</li>
</ul>
<p>FON envisions a future where feminist organizations thrive, where their voices are heard across communities and institutions, and where they have access to the flexible resources needed to adapt, innovate, and overcome challenges.</p>
<p>The initiative recognizes that meaningful social change requires strong grassroots organizations, collaborative networks, and sustained investments in feminist leadership.</p>
<h2>FON’s Mission and Vision</h2>
<p>At the heart of FON’s work is a commitment to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Eradicating gender-based violence</li>
<li>Advancing gender equality</li>
<li>Strengthening feminist movements</li>
<li>Promoting inclusivity and diversity</li>
<li>Building organizational resilience</li>
<li>Supporting sustainable social transformation</li>
</ul>
<p>The initiative seeks to create an environment where feminist organizations can operate effectively, advocate confidently, and influence policies and systems that affect women, girls, and marginalized communities.</p>
<h2>Funding Opportunities Available Through FON</h2>
<p>One of the key features of Feminist Opportunities Now is its commitment to providing support that meets the real-world needs of feminist organizations.</p>
<p>Unlike traditional funding models that often come with rigid restrictions, FON promotes the importance of flexible funding that allows organizations to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Respond quickly to emerging challenges</li>
<li>Adapt strategies to changing environments</li>
<li>Strengthen organizational sustainability</li>
<li>Expand advocacy and outreach efforts</li>
<li>Invest in leadership development</li>
<li>Build long-term institutional capacity</li>
</ul>
<p>This flexible approach enables organizations to focus on impact rather than administrative limitations.</p>
<h2>What Makes FON Unique?</h2>
<h3>1. Flexible Funding Support</h3>
<p>FON recognizes that organizations need funding structures that allow them to respond effectively to local realities and evolving challenges.</p>
<p>Flexible funding can support:</p>
<ul>
<li>Program implementation</li>
<li>Organizational development</li>
<li>Advocacy campaigns</li>
<li>Community engagement activities</li>
<li>Capacity-building initiatives</li>
<li>Operational sustainability</li>
</ul>
<h3>2. Capacity Strengthening</h3>
<p>Beyond financial support, FON invests in strengthening organizations through:</p>
<ul>
<li>Leadership development</li>
<li>Institutional capacity building</li>
<li>Strategic planning support</li>
<li>Organizational resilience initiatives</li>
<li>Knowledge sharing and learning opportunities</li>
</ul>
<p>These efforts help organizations become stronger, more sustainable, and better positioned to achieve their goals.</p>
<h3>3. Global Feminist Networks</h3>
<p>FON promotes collaboration and solidarity among feminist organizations across different countries and regions.</p>
<p>Participating organizations can benefit from:</p>
<ul>
<li>Cross-border networking opportunities</li>
<li>Shared learning experiences</li>
<li>Collaborative advocacy efforts</li>
<li>Exchange of best practices</li>
<li>Movement-building initiatives</li>
</ul>
<p>These connections help amplify collective impact and strengthen feminist movements globally.</p>
<h3>4. Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion</h3>
<p>FON celebrates diversity and seeks to ensure that organizations representing different communities, identities, and experiences are included within its network and support systems.</p>
<p>The initiative recognizes that diverse voices are essential for achieving meaningful and sustainable gender justice outcomes.</p>
<h2>Areas of Focus</h2>
<p>Organizations working in the following areas may find strong alignment with FON’s mission:</p>
<ul>
<li>Gender equality advocacy</li>
<li>Women’s rights promotion</li>
<li>Gender-based violence prevention and response</li>
<li>Feminist movement building</li>
<li>Youth empowerment</li>
<li>Digital rights and online safety</li>
<li>Leadership development</li>
<li>Community mobilization</li>
<li>Social justice initiatives</li>
<li>Inclusion and diversity programs</li>
</ul>
<h2>Impact of Feminist Opportunities Now</h2>
<p>FON has demonstrated its commitment to strengthening civil society organizations and feminist movements through:</p>
<ul>
<li>Subgranting support to civil society organizations</li>
<li>Capacity strengthening initiatives</li>
<li>Promotion of collaborative feminist action</li>
<li>Support for grassroots and community-led efforts</li>
</ul>
<p>Through these interventions, the initiative continues to contribute to stronger feminist ecosystems capable of driving meaningful social change.</p>
<h2>Why Feminist Funding Matters</h2>
<p>Feminist organizations often work on the frontlines of social transformation. They advocate for marginalized communities, challenge harmful norms, provide essential services, and hold institutions accountable.</p>
<p>Investing in these organizations leads to:</p>
<ul>
<li>Stronger communities</li>
<li>Improved gender equality outcomes</li>
<li>Reduced gender-based violence</li>
<li>Increased civic participation</li>
<li>More inclusive societies</li>
<li>Sustainable development progress</li>
</ul>
<p>By supporting feminist organizations, funding initiatives such as FON help ensure that gender justice movements have the resources and support needed to create lasting impact.</p>
<h2>How to Apply for FON Funding</h2>
<p>Organizations interested in exploring available funding opportunities through Feminist Opportunities Now should visit the official FON website to review current funding calls, eligibility requirements, and application procedures.</p>
<p><a href="https://feministnow.org/sub-granting/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><strong>APPLY HERE</strong></a></p>
<p>Applicants are encouraged to regularly monitor the platform for new opportunities, updates, events, and announcements.</p>
<h2>Deadline</h2>
<p>No specific application deadline has been publicly stated. Applications may be accepted on a rolling basis depending on available funding opportunities. Interested organizations are encouraged to apply as early as possible and regularly check the official website for updates.</p>
<h2>Conclusion</h2>
<p>Feminist Opportunities Now (FON) represents a powerful commitment to strengthening feminist movements worldwide. By combining flexible funding, capacity strengthening, networking opportunities, and a strong focus on gender justice, the initiative is helping organizations overcome barriers and accelerate progress toward equality.</p>
<p>Organizations working to eliminate gender-based violence, empower communities, and advance feminist causes should explore the opportunities available through FON and become part of a growing global movement dedicated to lasting social change.</p>
<p dir="ltr">For more information about this opportunity, visit <a href="https://feministnow.org/sub-granting/" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><strong>here</strong></a>.</p>

	<p>The Scholar Award is a one-time, competitive, merit-based award is intended to recognize and encourage academic excellence and achievement by women in doctoral-level programs. In addition to recognizing and encouraging excellence in higher education, these awards provide partial support for study and research for women who will make significant contributions in their varied fields of endeavor. All applicants are nominated by a local P.E.O. chapter.</p>

	<p><a href="https://storage.googleapis.com/peo-portal-static/4d954ea1053341149e83a1649aea2baa/941d46fb92ed4e7999de23491ed45eac/PSAPoliciesProceduresandGeneralInformation_202608_Final.pdf" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Download P.E.O. Scholar Awards Policies, Procedures and General Information</a></p>
<h3>Eligibility Requirements</h3>
<p>A woman is eligible for consideration for a P.E.O. Scholar Award if she:</p>
<ul>
<li>is nominated by a local chapter of the P.E.O. Sisterhood</li>
<li>is a citizen or legal permanent resident of the U.S. or Canada at the time of her nomination</li>
<li>at a minimum, has a bachelor’s degree</li>
<li>is within two years of her graduation date and has at least one full academic year of work remaining to complete her doctoral-level degree as measured from the time the first award payment is made (August 1). Those in a multiple-degree program (e.g., pursuing both an M.D. and a Ph.D.) must be within two years of completing the entire program from that date.</li>
<li>is enrolled in her program at an accredited U.S. or Canadian college or university. Study abroad is permitted provided the student is enrolled in a U.S. or Canadian postsecondary institution.</li>
<li>Is enrolled part time at the time of nomination, provided she is enrolled full time during the year of the award.</li>
</ul>
<p>The applications of individuals who satisfy these eligibility criteria will be evaluated on a nondiscriminatory basis without consideration of race, age, national origin, religious affiliation, disability or P.E.O. connection.</p>
<h3>Selection Criteria</h3>
<p>The Scholar Awards Board of Trustees evaluate applicants on the following:</p>
<ul>
<li>nominee's proposal</li>
<li>potential to make significant contributions in her field(s) of endeavor or to make a positive impact on society</li>
<li>recommendations from three university professors or professional mentors</li>
<li>evidence of scholarly activities (publications, presentations, patents, performances, etc.)</li>
<li>academic awards and honors (honor societies, scholarships, etc.)</li>
<li>academic record</li>
<li>career objectives</li>
</ul>
<p>It is often better to apply further into the doctoral program when evidence of achievement is more complete, giving a more thorough picture of an applicant’s professional work.</p>
<h3>Application Process</h3>
<p>Applicants are nominated by local P.E.O. chapters. The chapter nomination period is between August 20 and November 20 each year. After a chapter submits a nomination, the P.E.O. Executive Office will email the applicant instructions and a link to an online application.</p>
<p>The nominee is responsible for completing the online application packet and submitting it by the individually designated due date. Each nominee is given 45 days to complete the application. The nominee’s due date will appear on her application form.</p>
<p>The form requires information about research or an essay about the significance of the applicant’s chosen field, three letters of recommendation, evidence of scholarly activities, awards, academic records, career objectives, etc.</p>
<p>All nominees will be notified of their award status by May 1. Prospective scholars must agree to certain conditions of acceptance. Find full details in the policies and procedures.</p>
</div>

General Description and Purpose

Established in 1972, the Tuition Assistance Grant Program (VTAG) is designed to assist Virginia residents who attend accredited private, nonprofit colleges and universities in Virginia for other than religious training or theological education. The VTAG is authorized in § 23.1-628 of the Code of Virginia as the Tuition Assistance Grant Act.

Application Process

Applications may be acquired from the financial aid office of the private institution the student plans to attend. Completed applications must be submitted to the financial aid office of the institution on, or before, September 15 prior to the fall semester of enrollment. Applications submitted after September 15, but no later than December 1, will be considered for an award only if funds are available.

VTAG Applications

26-27 VTAG Application
26-27 TEP-VTAG Application

Eligibility

While this page does not cover all of the eligibility requirements, the basic criteria are:

  • Be a Virginia student as determined by 1) meeting domiciliary resident of Virginia as defined by the Code of Virginia §23.1-502 and augmented by the Domicile Guidelines, 2) meeting the military dependent requirements under § 23.1-505 or 3) meeting the Tuition Equity provision requirements under § 23.1-505.1;
  • Be enrolled full-time as an undergraduate, graduate, or professional student; and
  • Be enrolled at an eligible institution pursuing an eligible degree that is not in religious training or theological education.
    • Eligible graduate programs are limited to those in a health-related professional program, designated by the 51 series of programs under the NCES Classification of Instructional Programs.

Procedures for Attending SCHEV Meetings

All visitors to SCHEV must:

  • Sign in at the security desk on the first floor. Picture IDs will be required.
  • Anyone with a state-issued employee ID badge (including public institutions) may proceed to the 9th floor after signing in.
  • Anyone without a state-issued employee ID badge must wait for a staff member from SCHEV to escort them to the 9th floor after signing in. Upon leaving, all visitors without a state-issued employee ID badge must be escorted out of the building by a SCHEV staff member and must sign out at the security desk.

Note: Members of the public attending a meeting at SCHEV who do not have a state-issued employee ID badge should plan to arrive 20 minutes prior to the meeting and expect delays at the security desk. A SCHEV staff member will escort guests 10 minutes prior to the meeting. Anyone who arrives after the start of the meeting will need to remain at the security desk until a SCHEV staff member is available to escort them to the meeting.

Security desk hours are from 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM.

Applying for College

Everyone is different. Your background, interests and personality make you unique. When considering your future career and choice of college, it's easy to be influenced by what others think or say. Don't think of certain colleges as good or bad. Think of which would be best for you.

Depending on many factors, preparing for college can be a simple or a time-consuming process. This Explore section will give you and your family some of the tools you will need.

Virginia is home to many institutions of higher learning.

Public four-year schools can be large colleges and universities such as the the George Mason University, James Madison University, Old Dominion University, the University of Virginia, Virginia Commonwealth University and Virginia Tech, as well as smaller institutions such as Christopher Newport University, Longwood University, Radford University, the University of Mary Washington, U.Va.'s College at Wise, Virginia State University and Norfolk State.

Public two-year schools include the Virginia Community College System's 23 schools across Virginia and Richard Bland College.

Virginia's higher education also includes a wide range of private schools and colleges from Appalachian School of Law to Washington & Lee University. Some are nonprofit institutions, while others are for-profit.
